key_insight: Ranking-Aware Prompt Optimization (Ranking-PE) changes prompt search from accuracy-based scoring to pairwise ranking, so multimodal clinical models are optimized to rank true positives above negatives rather than just match labels.
clinical_relevance: This matters for imbalanced medical diagnosis tasks, where a model can look accurate while still failing to identify clinically important cases, whereas AUROC better reflects discrimination quality.
method: Replace per-example correctness with pairwise positive-vs-negative ordering in the prompt evolution score matrix.
Use the same reflective prompt-optimization pipeline, but select prompts by empirical AUROC instead of accuracy.
Apply the ranking objective to scores, reflection feedback, and final candidate selection without extra model calls.
evidence_signal: Across three MIMIC disease tasks, Ranking-PE outperformed accuracy-based prompt evolution by +5.8 AUROC points on fine-tuned Qwen3-VL-8B and +16.2 points on MedGemma-4B.
watch_item: The approach still depends on a strong medical visual backbone, so prompt search alone cannot compensate for weak multimodal pretraining or limited vision-encoder tuning.
paper_title: Ranking-Aware Prompt Optimization for Multimodal Clinical Diagnosis
